paragraphs.heading: How close to the original
paragraphs.edited: Why? Because it usually means it's been copied fewer times, and there's less chance of human error, to leave out a word, leave out a letter, leave out a line as you're copying, very honestly, to make that mistake. So intentional or unintentional error can happen in that window. It's several hundred years, the average age for your great classical writers, and many of them are an 800 to 1,000 year gap between the copies and the original. With the New Testament, we now go back within 50 years of the original. I mean, there's nothing else in history compares to it. And pretty soon, with a new manuscript to Mark, which will be released, I believe it'll take the New Testament back within 30 to 35 years.

paragraphs.heading: Thankful for the differences
paragraphs.edited: Now, I know some critics will push back and say, okay, you've got 5,800 Greek manuscripts, but when you compare the Greek manuscripts there are hundreds or thousands of differences across these manuscripts. Yes, but the great number is wonderful. I thank God for the great number. You say, what? Yes, because the great number represents the 5,800 manuscripts. You see, if one mistake was made, for example, they spelled John two different ways, or honor the American way, H-O-N-O-R, the British way, H-O-N-O-U-R, that's a discrepancy. But say in this manuscript right here, they spelled it H-O-N-O-U-R, a mistake, and in all these other manuscripts, they might have copied 8,000 manuscripts from there, they just repeated that same misspelling 8,000 times. But the reason I'm thankful there's more is because if we didn't have more, we wouldn't have the abundance of manuscripts to understand what Jesus said. And with all these manuscripts now, on the new technology and software, almost all those are going to be eliminated. But the majority of them are spelling and grammatical differences.

paragraphs.heading: Alleged discrepancies
paragraphs.edited: Now, I know some critics will push back and go, okay, wait a minute, all right, maybe the text has been reconstructed accurately to a degree, but when you look across, say, the Gospels, there are contradictions. One says there's one angel at the tomb, one says there's a young man, one says there's two angels. They describe the time that Jesus comes to the tomb differently. Well, you have to remember, we're 2,000 years removed. It's a different language, everything. So you're going to have alleged, I always put alleged, discrepancies. I think you can intellectually defend alleged discrepancies. I don't think you can intellectually defend discrepancies, because over the years one after another are being explained.

But what they later found out, there were two Jerichos, an old and a new, one inside the other. And so, yes, he was going into Jericho and going out of Jericho at the same time doing it. And so a lot of it is a misunderstanding of the grammar, of the meaning of the word. But this is why manuscripts and archaeological discoveries are so incredible. So I put it this way, you can intellectually defend an alleged discrepancy.
